raw_response:
Ahh, where do I start. I've been putting cotton on this little patch for — I can't even count how many years. 2.6 mu, that's all we've got. Me and the old lady work it together. The children are off in the city, they come back for picking if they can.

Let me think through this year like I do every year.

**Land prep.** Once it warms up in March I'll plow. I don't own a tractor — too small a piece to justify it. My nephew has a little walking tiller, I give him a bit of money for the fuel and he runs it over my field. Break up the clods, flatten it out. That's how I've always done it.

**Planting.** I wait till around the time of Grain Rain (谷雨), about April 20th. Soil needs to be warm or the seeds rot. My neighbor Old Wang tried to plant early two years ago to get a jump on things — cold snap hit and he had to replant half his field. I don't take that gamble. I buy seed from the same fellow at the agro-supply shop in town. A standard variety, nothing fancy. Maybe 50 yuan or so for the whole field.

**Fertilizer.** Before planting I put down two bags of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 stuff — across the whole field. That's two 50-kg bags, roughly. Spread it as I plow. Then when the plants start setting bolls around July, I topdress with about half a bag of urea. I don't weigh it out — I scoop it with the bowl I've always used. If the leaves look a little yellow I add a bit more. Young folks with more schooling do all that calculating from soil tests and what-not. I just go by what the plants look like, and what's worked for fifty years.

**Water.** I share a well with two neighbors. Cotton doesn't drink like wheat does. I water once when the flower buds form if it hasn't rained, and once more when the bolls are filling. That's usually enough. Pumping costs money — the electricity fee goes up every year, it seems. If the sky takes care of it, I don't turn the pump on.

**Pests.** Bollworm is the real trouble. I spray maybe three or four times through the summer. And I put down a herbicide early — I can't be crawling around pulling weeds at my age, my back is gone. The shop sells me what the other farmers are buying.

**Picking.** This is the hard part now. Cotton won't all open at once, so we go through the field two or three times from September into October. My wife and I pick what we can. Slow work. I don't hire pickers — too expensive for 2.6 mu, would eat all the profit. If my daughter can get off work for a few days, she comes back to help.

**What I expect.** Maybe 250 jin, 260 jin of lint per mu in a normal year. Some years less if bollworm is bad or the rain comes wrong. After fertilizer, seed, spray, water — not much money left. But this is what I know how to do.
